title: Inaccessible by Design: AIIB’s Complaint Mechanism
gist: Laure-Anne Courdesse argues the AIIB's Project-affected People's Mechanism is inaccessible by design: none of 45 complaints since 2019 passed admissibility, and 14 of 16 in 2026 were rejected, as the bank plans to double financing to about $20 billion annually by 2030.

insights.claim: Since its creation in 2019, none of the 45 complaints listed on the AIIB PPM's website as of September 15 has passed the admissibility stage, while peer mechanisms regularly proceed to dispute resolution or compliance review; one of the largest handled more than 60 cases in each of the last two financial years.
insights.speaker: Laure-Anne Courdesse
insights.so_what: AIIB's accountability machinery has never been tested, a governance and reputational risk for its projects and co-lenders.

insights.claim: Since the revised 2026 policy took effect, the PPM found 14 of 16 complaints inadmissible, with the other two (filed in May) still pending; the Mandalika complaint would be the 17th of 2026.
insights.speaker: Laure-Anne Courdesse
insights.so_what: The 2026 policy revision has not improved access.

insights.claim: On September 28, 108 Indigenous people from Lombok, Indonesia, filed a complaint over the AIIB-financed Mandalika Urban and Tourism Infrastructure Project alleging forced eviction, loss of farmland and livelihoods, and no consultation.
insights.speaker: Laure-Anne Courdesse
insights.so_what: Mandalika is a live test of whether the PPM will accept any complaint; a rejection would add to social-risk headlines on AIIB projects.

insights.claim: The PPM's entry requirements are more restrictive than peers: referring co-financed project complaints to the lead lender, narrow time limits for sovereign loan complaints, and required prior good-faith efforts with both the project-level grievance mechanism and bank management.
insights.speaker: Laure-Anne Courdesse
insights.so_what: Design features, not implementation, explain the rejections; fixes require policy change.

insights.claim: Requiring prior engagement at both the client and management level, and making complainants explain why it failed, is unique among peer mechanisms and puts the burden on those seeking redress.
insights.speaker: Laure-Anne Courdesse
insights.so_what: AIIB is an outlier among MDBs on accessibility.

insights.claim: In many AIIB borrowing countries, restrictive civic space and retaliation risks make prior engagement impractical, and the policy's retaliation exception has yet to be tested.
insights.speaker: Laure-Anne Courdesse
insights.so_what: Retaliation risk interacts with admissibility rules to block complaints in precisely the riskiest settings.

insights.claim: For compliance review, complainants must show the AIIB's noncompliance at the outset, yet the evidence sits in due diligence and supervision records they cannot see, so under a strict reading no complaint could qualify.
insights.speaker: Laure-Anne Courdesse
insights.so_what: Without compliance reviews, there are no findings to support remediation or learning.
insights.locator: For complaints seeking a compliance review

insights.claim: The AIIB, headquartered in Beijing with China its largest shareholder, began operating in 2016 and has grown to 111 members and nearly $70 billion invested in more than 350 projects across 40 economies.
insights.speaker: Laure-Anne Courdesse
insights.so_what: Scale of exposure grows without matching safeguards.

insights.claim: AIIB President Zou Jiayi announced at the Doha meeting plans to double annual financing to about $20 billion by 2030.
insights.speaker: Laure-Anne Courdesse
insights.so_what: A growing footprint raises the importance of accountability for project and reputational risk.

insights.claim: The authors urge new managing director Carmen Nonay to treat admissibility as a quick first step, trust complainants' accounts and use the PPM's unrestricted access to management information, and say the AIIB board should require policy changes if the PPM keeps struggling.
insights.speaker: Laure-Anne Courdesse
insights.so_what: Watch whether the pending complaints are admitted as a test of reform.

insights.claim: Because the PPM sits within the institution it reviews, its managing director may not feel sufficiently independent to adopt peer practice.
insights.speaker: Laure-Anne Courdesse
insights.so_what: Structural independence limits suggest board-level pressure is needed.
